content.overview: In-vitro shoots develop under high humidity, low mechanical stress and artificial nutrient conditions. Rooting and acclimatization must rebuild a functional root-shoot-water relationship before plantlets can tolerate normal cultivation environments.

vocabulary.definition: Outside sterile culture vessels in a greenhouse, growth room or other conventional environment.
Progressive adaptation of in-vitro plantlets to lower humidity, stronger light, airflow and substrate-based rooting conditions.
Temporary decline after transfer caused by abrupt changes in root function, water balance or environment.

sections.title: Rooting strategy can be integrated with acclimatization
sections.body: Recent cannabis research found that ex-vitro rooting can improve or streamline rooting and acclimatization for some genotypes, demonstrating that rooting strategy is a system choice rather than a fixed in-vitro requirement.

sections.title: Water balance changes abruptly after transfer
sections.body: Plantlets leaving culture face lower humidity and greater transpiration demand. Root function, leaf function, light and airflow must be increased gradually enough to avoid severe water deficit.

sections.title: Genotype-specific transition data matters
sections.body: Rooting and acclimatization success should be tracked by genotype and propagation treatment because multiplication success does not guarantee equivalent ex-vitro performance.

workedExamples: If shoots root well in vitro but collapse after transfer, evaluate humidity transition and root functionality rather than only rooting percentage.
If ex-vitro rooting performs better for one genotype, keep the genotype-specific workflow instead of forcing all lines through one route.
commonMistakes: Calling a plantlet successful as soon as roots are visible.
content.practicalApplication: Track survival at transfer, first week, second week and establishment. Record humidity transition, substrate, root method, genotype and new growth rather than only initial rooting percentage.
content.summary: Propagation success ends with stable ex-vitro growth, not with an in-vitro root. Rooting and acclimatization should be designed and measured as one connected transition.
